Our ethos

Listen First.

We start from the assumption that your team already knows what is wrong. Our job is to surface it, not to arrive with the answer.

  • The people doing the work hold the truth. Interviews, workshops and shadowing get it out; a template does not.
  • Validate before proposing. No premature optimisation, no solution looking for a problem.
  • Every finding is traceable to a person, a system, or a number — never to an assumption.

What we examine

Six things we look at.

Every engagement starts here. Nothing is designed until all six are understood — and understood from the people doing the work, not from a template.

Company Goals

Understand what the organisation is actually trying to achieve — and whether its parts agree.

  • Gather and validate goals across execs, ops, product, and field teams
  • Test that goals are aligned, measurable, and sequenced — not merely stated
  • Map goals to AI leverage points, system dependencies, and capability gaps

Systems

Establish what you run, how well you run it, and what it is capable of.

  • Inventory every system in use — core, satellite, and shadow IT
  • Mastery: assess whether each system is used to a fraction of its potential
  • Integration: identify what can, should, and already does connect
  • AI-readiness: evaluate data quality, accessibility, and automation potential

Pain Points

Find where the pressure is greatest and put a number on it.

  • Locate bottlenecks, delays, rework, and compliance exposure
  • Map who and what is at risk — roles, customers, revenue, safety, reputation
  • Quantify impact in cycle time, cost, error rate, and emotional load

Morale & Team Health

Treat team health as a measurable input to the redesign, not a soft afterthought.

  • Team Health Reports measuring wellbeing, psychological safety, clarity, cohesion, role fit, and readiness for change
  • Identify role misalignment — where responsibility and job description have parted ways
  • Surface the cultural blockers to transformation: fear, fatigue, confusion, siloing

Roles & Alignment

Put the right people in the right place for the operating model you are building toward.

  • Match capability, temperament, and workload to role
  • Redefine roles for an AI-enabled operating model
  • Clarify decision rights, ownership, and accountability

AI Enablement

Decide where AI genuinely earns its place, and prepare the ground for it.

  • Identify where AI meets a real need: automation, prediction, decision support, workflow augmentation
  • Prioritise opportunities by value, feasibility, and risk
  • Define AI-ready requirements: data, model behaviour, integration points
  • Build AI literacy across teams so adoption is not left to chance

Proof

We ran this playbook on ourselves.

Before advising anyone on AI transformation, we built and shipped one: a production system that drafts regulatory compliance documents for Australian road worksites, in a domain where a confident wrong answer is a safety problem rather than an embarrassment.

  • Never invent a safety-relevant value
  • Measure on two axes, never merge them
  • Corroborate to demote, never to overwrite
